newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia watchdog orders anti-laundering controls.
newsitem.headline: Colombia watchdog orders anti-laundering controls.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 4 Reuter - Colombia's Securities Superintendent said Friday he was ordering stricter controls after detecting money laundering operations totaling more than $40 million controls on the country's three stock markets last year.
Superintendent, Andres Uribe, said true scale of money laundering operations through the stock markets could be as high as $140 million per year but at present mechanisms did not exist to detect it.
"We must continue to step up controls so that funds from illicit activities do not enter the markets and get transferred from one sector to another," he told Reuters.

He said he would give the chairmen of the Bogota, Medellin and tiny Cali stock exchanges wider responsibilities to supervise accounts and to report suspicious transactions. That would include, Uribe said, the creation of data bases to chart stock movements and an anti-money laundering manual.
Last year, the securities superintendency suspended two brokerage firms for suspicious transactions worth about $40 million.
